title: Release Risk Runbook: coordinated blockers, rollback triggers, and incident comms
creator: Nina Patel
description: Create and socialize a coordinated launch risk runbook for runtime-1.21 that captures: release blockers, severity-based rollback triggers, step-by-step rollback procedures, prescriptive incident communications for internal and external audiences, and a postmortem/retrospective checklist. The runbook should be actionable for on-call SREs, product owners, and the GTM team and be available in Confluence and linked from release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook published to Confluence with stable URL and linked from release notes
Rollback triggers defined unambiguously with severity mapping and decision owners
At least three communication templates (internal incident, customer-facing alert, partner update) reviewed and approved by Legal and Support
Stakeholder contact list validated and on-call handoff process documented
Simulation tabletop exercise scheduled with SRE, Eng, PM, Support, and Comms prior to go-live
rollout_checklist: Confirm canary traffic policy configured for runtime-1.21: 1% for 2 hours, escalate if errors > 0.5%
Ensure prefix/KV cache migration test passed against canary nodes
Verify fallback model variants are pinned and available in each region
Tag release artifacts in GitHub and attach PRs to the runbook
Final sign-off from SRE lead, PM, and Head of Support 24 hours prior to release
known_blockers: ENG-8421: Kernel selection regression on 40K token sequences under 8-bit quantization (investigating)
ENG-8503: Autoscaler occasionally fails to add burst capacity when under simultaneous region failover
Dependency: External metrics exporter version mismatch in eu-west-1 cluster (roll-forward planned)
severity_based_rollback_triggers: sev-1: P99 latency increase > 2x for >10 minutes OR error rate > 5% for 5 minutes => immediate rollback unless mitigation accepted by SRE Director
sev-2: Sustained increase in 95th percentile latency 50-100% for >30 minutes => prepare rollback window and notify stakeholders
sev-3: Non-critical telemetry regressions (dashboards, cost spike) => monitor and schedule post-release fix; rollback optional
rollback_steps: Step 0: Decision owner (SRE Lead) confirms trigger conditions and escalates to PM and Head of Support
Step 1: Pause incoming canary and redirect traffic to previous stable model variant using routing policy 'release-fallback'
Step 2: Trigger automated rollback job in CI: deploy tag runtime-1.20-stable to all effected pools
Step 3: Invalidate problematic cache artifacts and restart serving processes if necessary
Step 4: Run smoke-tests: token-generation smoke test, embedding checksum, and critical route latency check
Step 5: Communicate status (internal then external) using templates in incident_comm_templates
Step 6: Schedule immediate retrospective with Eng, SRE, PM, Support, Comms within 48 hours
incident_comm_templates:
CUSTOMER OUTAGE TEMPLATE:
Subject: Service disruption affecting API responses — Redwood Inference
Dear {CustomerName},
We are currently investigating an issue affecting inference response times and errors for some requests. Our engineers have identified the cause and are executing an immediate mitigation plan. We may revert to the previous runtime version to restore service. We will update you within 30 minutes.
- Impact: {brief}
- Affected endpoints: {list}
- ETA for next update: 30 minutes
Sincerely,
Redwood Support

PARTNER STATUS UPDATE TEMPLATE:
Subject: Status update — Redwood runtime-1.21 release
Hello {PartnerName},
We wanted to provide a status update on the runtime-1.21 rollout. We have detected an operational degradation that may affect throughput in {region}. Our team has initiated rollback procedures and expect normalization within {ETA}. We will share a full postmortem after stabilization.
Regards,
Partner Ops

notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-03-05: Use conservative canary progression (1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24 hours) agreed by SRE and PM
Decision 2026-03-07: For sev-1 events, rollback is preferred over mitigation when impact > 5% of customer traffic
Tradeoff: Accept temporary availability drop when rolling back to ensure customer-facing correctness rather than toggling quantization profiles in production
